extracted.intended_audience: Medicare providers and administrators (acute care hospitals, CAHs, IOPOs/HCLs), Medicare contractors, and health policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the evaluative standards, statutory requirements, and procedural policies in the FY2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule preamble covering demonstrations (RCHD, FCHIP), episode payment models (TEAM, CJR-X), cost reporting and reconciliation, and related technical and administrative policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality requirement for Rural Community Hospital Demonstration (RCHD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 410A(c)(2) of Public Law 108-173, as amended, requires that the Secretary shall ensure that the aggregate payments made by the Secretary do not exceed the amount which the Secretary would have paid if the demonstration program under this section was not implemented (budget neutrality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed methodology: estimate additional payments made by the program for each participating hospital and adjust the national IPPS rates by an amount sufficient to account for the added costs. CMS applies budget neutrality across the payment system as a whole rather than only across participants. Previously incorporated a reconciliation component (difference between estimated and actual costs) into future budget neutrality offsets; for FY2027 CMS proposes not to apply a budget neutrality offset due to unavailable finalized cost reports and instead proposes applying FY2027 and FY2028 estimated costs in FY2028, and invites public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and treatment of budget neutrality offsets when cost estimates are unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When finalized estimated costs for a demonstration are not available at the time of the proposed rule, CMS may defer applying a budget neutrality offset and instead propose to apply combined estimates in a subsequent year's rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For FY2027 CMS is not able to finalize estimated RCHD costs; therefore CMS is not proposing a budget neutrality offset for FY2027 and proposes to apply both FY2027 and FY2028 estimated demonstration costs into the FY2028 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule. Consistent with past practice, CMS would include differences between estimated and actual costs from prior years in the offset calculation. CMS invites public comments on this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality requirement and contingency approach for FCHIP Demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 123(g)(1)(B) of Pub. L. 110-275 requires the demonstration be budget neutral: the Secretary shall ensure aggregate payments do not exceed the amount estimated would have been paid absent the demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS selected CAHs with the goal of maintaining budget neutrality on its own terms and adopted a contingency plan: if analysis (claims, cost reports, other data) shows increases in Medicare payments under the demonstration are not sufficiently offset elsewhere, CMS will recoup additional expenditures attributable to the demonstration through a reduction in payments to all CAHs nationwide. Rationale: small scale of demonstration makes limiting reductions to participants infeasible. CMS may update/modify the budget neutrality methodology when extension-period data become available; CMS did not propose a budget neutrality payment offset for FY2027 for FCHIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and eligibility policy for FCHIP demonstration participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the 10 CAHs that participated in the initial FCHIP Demonstration period are eligible to participate during the extension period; among those eligible CAHs, participation in the extension period is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the extension period five elected to participate; selection aimed to maintain demonstration budget neutrality and to implement three intervention services (telehealth, ambulance, SNF/NF services). CMS may monitor and recoup costs across all CAHs if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and accountability structure of the Transforming Episode Accountability Model (TEAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAM is a mandatory episode-based payment model testing financial accountability for specified episode categories (e.g., CABG, LEJR, major bowel procedure, surgical hip/femur fracture treatment, spinal fusion) to reduce Medicare expenditures while preserving or enhancing quality of care under section 1115A authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under TEAM participants continue to bill under traditional FFS; participants may receive reconciliation payments if performance-year FFS expenditures are less than the reconciliation target price, subject to a quality adjustment. Track 1: upside-only (no downside risk). Tracks 2 and 3: two-sided risk (participants accountable for spending above or below target, subject to quality adjustment resulting in reconciliation payment or repayment). CMS anticipates TEAM will incentivize care redesign strategies (e.g., improved discharge planning, post-hospital follow-up, coordination with post-acute providers). CMS proposed updates (e.g., include spinal fusion MS-DRGs, changes to normalization factor and update factors) intended to improve pricing accuracy and maintain episode volume; CMS does not anticipate these proposed changes materially altering previously estimated Medicare savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial impact estimation and stance on TEAM proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare savings estimates for TEAM were previously projected across five performance years; CMS believes the FY2027 proposed refinements would not materially change the Medicare savings estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provided prior numerical estimates (e.g., net payments and repayments over 2026–2030) and notes that certain RFI topics (voluntary participation, adding ASC episodes) could affect Medicare savings; generally, financial impacts are based on proposed policies and not updated based on RFI responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X model accountability and payment safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X is a mandatory episode-based payment model holding anchor hospitals accountable for spending during a lower extremity joint replacement episode; participants are subject to two-sided financial risk and could receive reconciliation payments or owe repayments based on spending and quality performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial safeguards proposed: cap outlier high-cost episode spending, apply stop-gain and stop-loss limits to prevent extreme reconciliation or repayment amounts, and exempt hospitals meeting the low volume threshold from accountability for insufficient-volume episodes. Participants may earn performance-based payments by reducing expenditures and meeting specified quality metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measurement and eligibility for reconciliation payments in CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposed adoption and public reporting of five quality measures for CJR-X: two complications measures, two patient experience survey measures, and one patient reported outcome measure; participants must meet proposed quality performance standards to qualify to receive a reconciliation payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures are intended to ensure continuous measurement of care quality and monitor beneficiary safety. CMS proposes these measures in section X.C.2.e and ties reconciliation eligibility to meeting quality thresholds (see X.C.2.f.(5).(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X baseline, pricing assumptions, and sensitivity testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline episode spending is projected using 2024 actual spending trended for price and enrollment changes; assumptions include use of Trustees Report projections for price updates, no change to 2024 volume/intensity, and assumed behavior changes (e.g., 1 percent reduction in episode spending in year 1 maintained forward).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS sensitivity-tested savings assumptions (Table K-CL-02). Assumed average quality-adjusted discount is 1.3 percent. Financial impacts assume retrospective trend adjustment isn't capped (difference between prospective and retrospective trend <3%). CMS notes that reductions in episode spending can lower target prices but increase costs from stop-loss limits, moderating overall savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary protections and monitoring under CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X does not affect beneficiary freedom of choice under section 1802; eligible beneficiaries receiving services from CJR-X participants would not have the option to opt out of inclusion in the model; hospitals may recommend but may not restrict beneficiaries to certain providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections include: requiring providers to supply beneficiaries with written information about model design and Medicare rights; monitoring claims data (e.g., compare hospital case mix to pre-model baseline) to detect systematic exclusion/avoidance of complex/high-cost patients; audits if claims analysis indicates inappropriate changes; a 90-day episode length to reduce risk of delayed care; counting certain outlier costs in the 30-day post-episode window as adjustments against reconciliation/repayment to limit incentives to delay care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to reconcile non-renal organ acquisition costs for IOPOs and HCLs and establish non-renal SACs/testing rates
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to reconcile non-renal organ acquisition costs for independent organ procurement organizations (IOPOs) and histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), and to require the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) to establish, adjust if necessary, and publish non-renal standard acquisition charges (SACs) and non-renal testing rates, with a proposed 1-year delay in implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated fiscal impacts (e.g., $0 in FY2027 due to delay, $100M in FY2028, $500M over FY2027–2031). Data sources: Office of the Actuary used 2024 cost report data. CMS does not have required data to estimate HCL impacts. CMS follows standardized cost reporting definitions under 42 CFR 413.20(a). CMS invites public comment on burden estimates and staffing assumptions in Collection of Information section (XII.B.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting burden and cost estimates for IOPOs/HCLs (Form CMS-216-94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current reporting: 94 Medicare certified OPOs/HCLs file Form CMS-216-94 annually with an estimated average burden per OPO/HCL of 45 hours (30 hours recordkeeping, 15 hours reporting). For this proposal CMS estimates no additional recordkeeping burden but an additional reporting burden of 10 hours per OPO/HCL and additional annual reporting cost of $785.40 per OPO/HCL (using BLS hourly wage for accounting professionals doubled to account for fringe/overhead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total reporting burden cost estimated at $73,828 (94 × $785.40). Because of proposed 1-year delay, costs would not occur until FY2028 if finalized. CMS invites comment on hours estimate and staffing used to compile cost report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed reasonable cost reimbursement policy changes and codification
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to change certain existing policy and codify longstanding Medicare reasonable cost reimbursement policies applicable to providers reimbursed on a reasonable cost basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes these proposals would not result in additional costs or increased burden, may alleviate burden by clarifying cost reporting policies, and could result in cost savings via increased payment accuracy, though it lacks sufficient data to estimate amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification of cost allocation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to codify cost allocation principles applicable to all providers to clarify how overhead costs should be allocated for Medicare payment purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes codification would not increase Medicare program costs or provider burden because providers are already required to follow current cost reporting instructions; may result in payment accuracy improvements leading to savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification of discretionary Administrator review for appeals under §413.420(g) for IOPOs and HCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to codify the discretionary Administrator review of CMS reviewing official determinations with respect to appeals under §413.420(g) for IOPOs and HCLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes there would be no additional costs to the Medicare program and no increased burden on providers as a result of this codification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections and clarifications to §§412.116(c) and 413.404(b)(3)(ii)(A) and (C)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes technical corrections or clarifications to regulatory text at §§412.116(c) and 413.404(b)(3)(ii)(A) and (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states these clarifications and corrections would not create additional costs to the Medicare program or increased provider burden.
